clue.text: Saw mistake in the lady's cable

indicators.note: in says the jumbled letters go inside the word for the lady's

parts.note: the lady's is the possessive her

indicators.note: a mistake garbles things, so the letters of saw are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone has made an error cutting a woman's cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb or a tool, but it is just three letters for 'mistake' to jumble (AWS).
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope or cable used for mooring or towing ships.

clue.text: He designed a water container

parts.note: a dam holds back and contains water

explanation.surface: Someone created a vessel for holding water.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Adam was the celebrated eighteenth-century Scottish architect and designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Adam was a famous Georgian architect and interior designer, so he is a man who designed.

clue.text: Dish for turning apples out

indicators.note: turning the letters over and around rearranges them into a new order

explanation.surface: A bowl used for tipping out apples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges the nine letters of APPLES OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A soup plate is a deep dish with a broad rim for serving soup.

clue.text: Rank card in order

indicators.note: putting letters in a new order means rearranging them, so card and in are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Ranking a card within a sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a verb about arranging cards, but it is the adjective meaning foul-smelling. 'order' rearranges CARD IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means rotten or foul-smelling, a synonym of rancid.

clue.text: Weed on arch bent over canal basin

indicators.note: something bent is out of shape, so the letters of arch are twisted round

parts.note: a lock is the enclosed basin on a canal where water levels change

explanation.surface: A weed growing on a curved bridge above a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' makes CHAR from the arch; in an across clue 'over' simply places it before the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlock is wild mustard, a common yellow-flowered weed of fields.

clue.text: Succeeded with the one act mother produced

indicators.note: produced suggests the letters are worked up into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A one-act play was staged along with a piece about a mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges the fifteen letters of THE ONE ACT MOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed a monarch is to take their place, that is, to become the reigning sovereign.

clue.text: Right cricket ground applied first for confirmation

indicators.note: first places the abbreviation for applied ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: app. is a standard abbreviation for applied
the Oval is a famous Test cricket ground in south London

explanation.surface: The correct sports ground was used first to confirm something.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; 'first' puts APP (app. = applied) before R and OVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Approval of a plan is its official endorsement or confirmation.

clue.text: Popular golfer, but somewhat slow

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A well-liked golfer who plays rather slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles popuLAR GOlfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical direction for a slow, broad tempo.

clue.text: Account king gives to historian

parts.note: a chronicle is a historical account of events
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch hands a written record to a scholar of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicler is someone who records events in sequence, a kind of historian.

clue.text: Tree in container seen in album, perhaps

indicators.note: seen in says one piece appears inside the other
perhaps marks album as a possible arrangement, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: an urn is a vase-like container

explanation.surface: A tree in a pot appears in a photo album, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' makes LABUM from the album, and 'seen in' splits it after LAB.
explanation.definitionFit: The laburnum is a small tree with hanging yellow flowers and poisonous seeds.

clue.text: Turn up rare set of ornaments

indicators.note: turn tells us to spin the letters round into a new order

explanation.surface: An unusual set of jewels turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reads as a phrase meaning appear; 'Turn' alone rearranges UP RARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parure is a matching set of jewels or ornaments worn together.

clue.text: Precise moment to stop race

parts.note: a point in time is a precise moment
a full stop is also called a point

explanation.surface: An exact time at which to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is an amateur steeplechase for hunting horses, popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A point-to-point is a cross-country horse race run over a marked course.

clue.text: He soon learns about solar patch

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of solar patch are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone quickly finds out about a sunny spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SOLAR PATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An apt scholar is a quick learner, one who picks things up easily.

clue.text: Hebrew measure used by the Pharaohs

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ancient Hebrew unit of measure employed by Egyptian kings.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles thE PHAraohs.
explanation.definitionFit: An epha (ephah) is an ancient Hebrew dry measure of about a bushel.

clue.text: Negotiate across catwalk

parts.note: trans- is the Latin prefix meaning across

indicators.note: walk suggests the letters of cat wander about into a new order

explanation.surface: Bargaining over a fashion runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catwalk' splits in two: CAT is rearranged by 'walk' to ACT, after TRANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact business is to carry it out or negotiate a deal.

clue.text: Put off for a while, like old socks?

definitions.meaning: old-fashioned socks were held up by suspenders, so they hung from them

explanation.walkthrough: Sock suspenders were garters that held up men's socks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspended is postponed, and also hanging, held up from above.

clue.text: One who opposed something, or supports

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: an object is a thing, something

explanation.surface: A dissenter or someone who props things up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supports' puts OR below OBJECT.
explanation.definitionFit: An objector is a person who raises objections, someone opposing a proposal.

clue.text: Gather in island dining room on return

indicators.note: on return means the whole combined piece is read backwards
in places the dining room inside the island

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
a mess is a dining room for service personnel

explanation.surface: People congregate in a mess on an island after coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather' looks like part of the surface story; 'in' makes ELBMESSA, which 'on return' turns round in full.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather or come together in one place.

clue.text: Favourites return to stage

indicators.note: return means the word is turned back and read the other way

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Favoured performers come back to the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a stage in a process.

clue.text: Game to saucy prince

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union
pert means cheeky or saucy

explanation.surface: Playing a game with a cheeky royal.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Rupert of the Rhine was a royalist commander in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert is the name of a famous prince, Rupert of the Rhine, and of others.

clue.text: Free hours with teacher in school

indicators.note: free means released from fixed form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Time off spent with a teacher at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' rearranges HOURS and TEACHER together; Charterhouse is an English public (private boarding) school in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Charterhouse is a well-known independent school in Godalming, Surrey.

clue.text: Speaks angrily about gears

indicators.note: about means turned around, so gears is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shouts about car gears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges GEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: To rage is to speak or act with violent anger.

clue.text: Previously at church

parts.note: on can mean at, as in on time or at the time
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Formerly at a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past, formerly or previously.

clue.text: Sudden exit from the airport?

definitions.meaning: a plane journey departing from an airport

explanation.definitionFit: A flight is both a fleeing and a journey by air leaving an airport.

clue.text: Deliveries executed, but carried too far

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by a bowler
done means carried out or executed

explanation.surface: Goods were delivered and the job completed, but excessively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' reads as parcels; in cricket an OVER is six balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdone means exaggerated or taken to excess.

clue.text: Keep out of pickle

definitions.meaning: to keep something safe or maintain it
a jam, pickle or other food kept in jars

explanation.definitionFit: A preserve is a jarred food such as jam or pickle, and to preserve is to keep.

clue.text: Did he make hay in the RAF?

definitions.meaning: a person or machine that spreads hay to dry
Arthur ... was a Marshal of the Royal Air Force in the Second World War

explanation.definitionFit: A tedder spreads cut grass for haymaking, and Lord Tedder led the RAF.
